$comment: Canonical journey-audit findings. Generated once from the capture run and tracked so `npm run check` is reproducible from a clean checkout. `scripts/journey-atlas-gate.mjs` is the only reader; edit findings here, then run `node scripts/journey-atlas-gate.mjs --fix`.

personas.persona: Novice — heard "Airship runs AI in your browser with no account", knows ChatGPT, does not know what a vault, attestation, posture or profile is. Wants to ask a question and get a real answer, then come back tomorrow.
personas.headline: Airship's honesty machinery is genuinely excellent in prose but broken in state: on a cold first open the only warning-coloured line on screen falsely tells a brand-new user they already lost a conversation, and a single browser refresh silently destroys everything they typed while the recents list and the "All conversations" audit surface both report that nothing is missing.

journeys.name: First open — "what is this, and can I just ask something?"
Ask something before connecting — "is this thing actually answering me?"
Connect Chutes — the flow, as far as it goes with no credentials
Come back tomorrow — the conversation is gone and nothing says so

personas.persona: power-user — weeks in Airship, keyboard-first, three profiles (General/Research/Developer), many conversations, wants speed and wants to branch a thread without losing the thread
personas.headline: Airship's expert layer exists and works — eight `g` chords, ⌘K, ⌘\, per-profile drafts, real profile silos — but it is taught nowhere except inside the palette it can't teach you to open, and the one power move that matters most (Edit & branch) announces "Carrying 4 ancestor messages" onto a screen with zero messages on it.

journeys.name: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
Switch profiles mid-thought without losing the thread
Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow

personas.persona: keyboard-a11y — a keyboard-only screen-reader user, mouse never touched, driving Airship at 1440x900 and 390x844 with Tab / Shift+Tab / arrows / Enter / Escape only, and reading state through accessible names and live-region text changes rather than pixels.
personas.headline: Airship's keyboard *mechanics* are unusually good — a working roving-tabindex rail, real skip links, a properly trapped and `inert`-backed approval dialog — but almost nothing that *happens* is spoken: the reply, the error, the permission denial and the write receipt all reach the screen and never reach the announcement channel, so a screen-reader user can operate every control in the product and still not know what it did.

journeys.name: Cold start: orient and reach everything with Tab alone
Ask a question and listen for the answer
Run a command that fails, and find out that it failed
Decide a capability request: let the agent write a file

personas.persona: Researcher holding a long investigation across many sources — accumulating notes over weeks, needing to re-find something learned earlier and cite exactly where it came from, then carry that citation back into a conversation without losing their place.
personas.headline: Airship's Memory is a beautifully instrumented read-only *inspector* — every hit carries digests, revisions and scores — but it is not a place a researcher can accumulate into, browse, or return from: the product's own suggested query returns "No memory matched", a note you explicitly remember is silently gone after one reload while the header still says "Private · on-device", and jumping from a hit back to the conversation drops you 2,505px past the sentence you searched for.

journeys.name: Find what I noted last week, and get from the hit back to the source and the conversation
Capture something I just learned so it survives the week
Prove where an answer came from, then get back to the thread

personas.persona: privacy-first — a security-conscious operator who will not send anything anywhere they cannot verify, and who came for the trust model rather than the chat
personas.headline: Airship's trust surfaces are unusually honest at rest but lie in motion and at the moment of commitment: the Connection page asserts "Nothing has been sent yet." for 4,375 ms while the API key is actually in flight to two Chutes hosts, and the Vault ceremony tells you to save a recovery key that provably cannot restore anything after you lose the browser profile.

journeys.name: Audit every trust claim on screen and take the proof away with me
Stand up a Vault and prove it will actually survive
Verify what leaves the device before trusting it with a credential

personas.persona: Developer using Airship as a working environment — files, editor, terminal, Git — expecting the five surfaces to be one workflow.
personas.headline: Editing, diffing, staging and committing in Airship genuinely works and is beautiful, but the three links a developer relies on after the work is done — permission that names what it is changing, an audit that admits the commit happened, and persistence that keeps it — all quietly fail, and the terminal is a second, silently divergent copy of the same workspace with a different absolute path.

journeys.name: Change a file and land it in Git
Use the terminal against the workspace I am editing
Prove the commit happened, and still have it tomorrow

personas.persona: mobile — someone whose only device is a phone (390x844, touch only, no hover, no keyboard, flaky mobile data)
personas.headline: Airship's mobile *shell* is genuinely first-class — the bottom bar, the More sheet, the approval dock and the whole Vault recovery ceremony all work under a thumb — but the content panes still carry desktop-width and desktop-time assumptions, so on a phone the product breaks its own honesty rule: it clips the evidence it tells you to read, and it prints durability and credential verdicts that the same screen disproves.

journeys.name: Make this thing actually answer me — connecting a model from a phone on patchy data
Descend to the machinery from a train seat — files, diff, terminal, and the receipt that proves it
Make my work survive closing the tab — the Vault ceremony and the reload that follows

personas.persona: Returning — someone who used Airship two days ago and comes back to finish a half-remembered conversation. Driven at 1440x900 and 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch) against the production preview at localhost:4173, using persistent Chromium profiles so a "cold open" is a real browser restart, not a reload. Scripts and screenshots: /Users/chrisk/airship/.ui-capture/journeys/ret-*.mjs, RF-*.png, RN-*.png, RM-*.png, RV-*.png.
personas.headline: Airship reopens rather than resumes: in the default (no-Vault) configuration a returning person's entire Tuesday is gone with zero acknowledgement that anything ever existed, and even with the encrypted Vault active the product's own address bar tells them "That conversation existed only in page memory and did not survive the reload" about a conversation it has just restored and lists as "Ready to resume".

journeys.name: Come back to Tuesday's thread with nothing configured (the default path)
Come back with the encrypted Vault active — resume vs reopen
Come back after walking away mid-approval

personas.persona: failure-recovery — deliberately broke turns, connections, durability and reloads, then measured whether the person's work and the truth survived
personas.headline: Airship's failure states are beautifully written but structurally unfinished: the recovery action the error card promises ("Retry is available.") is disabled for every un-Vaulted user, the footer claims "PARTIAL RESPONSE KEPT" when nothing was kept, and after a reload the composer says the conversation "did not survive" while the rail lists it and a full, honest resume record sits three clicks away.

journeys.name: The turn just failed — get me back to work without retyping
I reloaded while it was answering — where did my conversation go?
It is still thinking — wait, it says I cancelled it

personas.persona: long-session — someone eight hours into one working day in Airship: one long conversation, a workspace, a terminal that has been open since morning, and a habit of firing off questions faster than they get answered.
personas.headline: Airship survives volume better than it survives a refresh: 180 turns cost nothing in latency (p50 1,557 ms at turn 1 and at turn 180) but the chat surface spends the entire day claiming "Persisting turn intent", "Local kernel ready" and "⌗ 1079 events" over a browser storage estimate that never moves off 4,503,947 bytes — and one reload replaces the day with "General conversation · 2 events" and a past-tense apology.

journeys.name: The eight-hour conversation
The backlog: firing questions faster than they are answered
The terminal that has been open since morning
Hour eight on the phone

personas.persona: COMPLETENESS CRITIC — the person none of the ten modelled: someone on their SECOND tab, second conversation, second profile and second visit, who reconfigures the agent mid-conversation and expects the product to keep up. Coverage audit first: across all ten personas the least-worked chain links were **recovery** (only ever tested as "does the error card offer a verb", never "does the verb do anything"), **continuation across a configuration change**, and **permission/proof for non-chat surfaces**. Four routes were opened by nobody: `#skills`, `#capabilities`, `#account`, `#context`. And nobody ever ran two Airships at once — which is what a browser-first product is for.
personas.headline: Airship is built for one tab, one conversation and one configuration at a time: open a second tab and the product renders "Open in another tab · page-memory state is not shared" and "Your last visit was not kept … the browser releases when the page closes" in the same frame — it detects the live peer tab and simultaneously reports that peer's work as destroyed — and the same one-of-everything assumption makes the Capabilities page's primary amber button, "Activate in Chat", silently abandon the conversation you are in while activating nothing.

journeys.name: The second tab — "I'll just open Airship again in another tab"
Changing what the agent is, mid-conversation — Capabilities and Skills
A route failed to load once, and never loaded again
The four routes nobody opened — Skills, Capabilities, Account, and the address with no door

Source: /Users/chrisk/airship/src/ui/app.tsx:2025.

findings.evidence: Verbatim on the Chutes card: "Chutes sign-in is not available in this build." and the OAuth tab reads "OAuth — Unavailable in this build". The only path offered is "Paste an API key to connect." with "Held only in page memory. Don't have one? Create a key at chutes.ai → API keys ↗". Confirmed non-persistent: on a second tab in the same namespace, `{"keyVal":"","chip":"No model connected · 5 ready"}`.

findings.journey: Connect Chutes — the flow, as far as it goes with no credentials
findings.what: A syntactically-shaped but entirely fake key advances the flow into a green success banner, a lock chip reading like an established session, and a priced model picker — because the catalog reads are unauthenticated. The credential is not checked until a separate commit 10 s later.
findings.evidence: With `cpk_notarealkey000000`: green banner "13 encrypted-inference candidates found.", chip "🔒 Chutes API key · direct session", model "Qwen/Qwen3-32B-TEE ✦ privacy-first recommendation", "AVAILABILITY hot", "INPUT / OUTPUT $0.104 / $0.416 USD per million tokens". Network during discovery: `GET https://llm.chutes.ai/v1/models auth=no`, `GET https://api.chutes.ai/chutes/?include_public=true… auth=no`, `GET https://api.chutes.ai/chutes/utilization auth=no` — all 200, none carrying the key. Screenshot /Users/chrisk/airship/.ui-capture/journeys/novtd-keyfail.png.

findings.journey: Connect Chutes — the flow, as far as it goes with no credentials
findings.what: The connection chip counts provider integrations as "ready" when none of the five can be used without credential work the user must do outside Airship.
findings.evidence: Chip text "No model connected · 5 ready", aria-label "No model connected · 5 ready. Connect one, or several at once." On the same page: Chutes needs a chutes.ai key, OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI each require ticking "I accept this browser-direct credential boundary" plus a pasted key, and Ollama/LM Studio show "Check this machine" with nothing running. Measured identically at 1440×900 and 390×844.

Rail after reload: "● General conversation / No messages yet / 1:45 PM". The header count reads "General conversations 1" both before and after. Conversation id changed `21feb15b-f93b-4374-9bea-4c51bb0aeab3` → `2ac0bb75-6961-4d20-b99a-2d549c2f5c35`.

findings.journey: Come back tomorrow — the conversation is gone and nothing says so
findings.what: The audit surface that exists to prove what happened reports a clean, resumable shelf immediately after four messages and two receipts were destroyed.
findings.evidence: "All conversations" verbatim after the reload: "1 conversation … General conversation just now Active 2 events general airship/demo-v1 … Structure passed Ready to resume 0 receipts … RUNTIME RECORD Manifest pins and transcript · 0 messages". Nothing records that conversation `21feb15b…` ever existed or was discarded.

findings.journey: Come back tomorrow — the conversation is gone and nothing says so
findings.what: Nothing on the chat surface warns that conversations are not being saved, before or after the fact; the word never appears where the person is typing.
findings.evidence: Scanned every leaf text node on the chat view for /durable|persist|save this conversation|keep|survive|adopt|sync/i — result: `DURABILITY LANGUAGE ON SCREEN: []`. The only statement of the fact, "Ephemeral · this page only — This session journal exists only in page memory. Nothing is synced.", is inside a popover behind a 44 px unlabelled chip whose visible content is a bare "○".

findings.journey: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
findings.what: Nothing on screen teaches ⌘K; the chord lives only in a hover tooltip
findings.evidence: On a fully loaded chat route, `document.body.innerText.includes("⌘K")` === false and `.includes("⌘\\")` === false. The only carrier is `title="Command palette · ⌘K"` on the topbar button (src/ui/app.tsx:8509) — invisible to touch and to anyone who does not hover a bare ⌘ glyph.

findings.journey: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
findings.what: There is no shortcut sheet anywhere: no `?`, no F1, no Preferences section, and the palette cannot even find the word
findings.evidence: `?`, `F1`, `Shift+/` each produced dialogs `[]`. Preferences dialog innerText tested against /keyboard|shortcut|chord/ → false (its sections are "Active profile approvals / Color mode / Type scale / Density / Corners / Tool steps / Body font / STORAGE Durability"). Palette queries "shortcut", "keyboard" and "chord" each returned "No matching destination or command."

findings.journey: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
findings.what: The palette is navigation-only — it holds no verbs, so every action still requires menu archaeology
findings.evidence: Palette query "new conversation" → "No matching destination or command."; "switch" → "No matching destination or command."; "retry" → "No matching destination or command."; "rename" → only "/move-file". Meanwhile the live shell exposes buttons titled "New conversation", "Rename conversation", "Fork", "Retry" and "Edit & branch".

findings.journey: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
findings.what: With an empty query the palette lists zero conversations, so ⌘K ↵ cannot return you to what you were doing
findings.evidence: Placeholder reads "Go to a view, session, or command…", yet the unfiltered list is 15 destinations then slash commands — no session rows. Typing "Alpha" does find "Alpha topic about vector search · Recent session · 70338e22… · Sessions", proving the source exists but is gated behind guessing a title.

findings.journey: Reach any surface without leaving the home row
findings.what: Keyboard focus inside the terminal silently swallows navigation chords with nothing on screen saying which keys the page still owns
findings.evidence: After clicking the xterm surface, focus = `TEXTAREA.xterm-helper-textarea aria=Terminal input`; pressing `g` then `s` left `location.hash === "#terminal"`. Tab → "Terminal input" (consumed); Shift+Tab → "Close terminal tab" (escapes). The terminal's own help text explains git and durability but never focus: "Interactive jsh process running inside this page's WebContainer. Input history · 0 Audit lineage · 1".

findings.journey: Switch profiles mid-thought without losing the thread
findings.what: There is no keyboard path to the thing a multi-profile user does most
findings.evidence: Tabbing from the transcript, the "Agent profile" control is the 24th tab stop (order ended: … "Skip to conversation", "Skip to composer", "Open session", "Runtime trust for this browser tab…", "Connect a model", "Open command palette", "Open Preferences", "Open proof", "Agent profile"). NAVIGATION_JUMPS (src/ui/platform-shell.tsx:219) binds no profile chord, and palette query "switch" → "No matching destination or command."

findings.journey: Switch profiles mid-thought without losing the thread
findings.what: A terminal declares itself unusable and then keeps working
findings.evidence: After a General → Research → General round trip, the General terminal buffer reads "Airship changed terminal workspace authority; this terminal requires restart." — and the very next line, typed after that warning, is "❯ echo STILL-ALIVE" followed by "STILL-ALIVE". A power user will read the sentence, watch it execute anyway, and stop believing the warning.

findings.journey: Switch profiles mid-thought without losing the thread
findings.what: Live work left behind in another profile is disclosed nowhere in the profile you are standing in
findings.evidence: While in Research with General's PTY still alive (its tab still reads "Running Terminal 1" on return), the only global process reading is the rail's "0 Idle · No execution run is in flight. Peak 0 this page." A body-text scan for /another profile|other profile/ returned "none".

findings.journey: Switch profiles mid-thought without losing the thread
findings.what: The completion signal for a profile switch is visible for roughly a sixth of a second and is then overwritten by an unrelated storage warning
findings.evidence: "Research cockpit started" sampled present at t=51/103/154ms and gone at t=205ms, replaced in the same slot by "Local Device Vault needs a saved recovery key before first use".

findings.journey: Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow
findings.what: A branch opens looking like a brand-new empty conversation while carrying hidden ancestor context into the model
findings.evidence: Edit & branch on turn 3: notice "Carrying 4 ancestor messages; none omitted." and header "Continued from the source conversation at event 17 · 4 ancestor messages carried, 0 omitted." — with `document.querySelectorAll('.message').length === 0` and the newcomer empty state on screen: "Open a terminal · Real processes in this tab, no account", "Browse the workspace", "Connect a model · Only chat needs this".

findings.journey: Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow
findings.what: The carried context is unreadable anywhere, including the audit surface that should hold it
findings.evidence: The same branch's row in All conversations reads "RUNTIME RECORD Manifest pins and transcript · 0 messages", and after sending one turn it reads "· 2 messages" — never 4 or 6. The only trace of the inherited messages is the count sentence and "Event 2 · session.fork.context.seeded · sha256:VUd6Uqu7…".

findings.journey: Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow
findings.what: Branches name themselves by concatenation, so different branches of one conversation become indistinguishable rows
findings.evidence: Two Edit & branch operations on different turns of the same conversation both produced the title "Q1 about retrieval · edit"; two retries produced "Base question · retry" then "Base question · retry · retry", and a further edit produced "Base question · retry · retry · edit". In the list column the title element renders 119px of 353px of text, so both branch rows read "Retrieval quality for t…" and the distinguishing suffix is exactly what is clipped.

findings.journey: Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow
findings.what: A conversation row in All conversations does not open the conversation — not by click, double-click, or Enter
findings.evidence: With hash "#sessions": single click → "#sessions"; double click → "#sessions"; focus + Enter → "#sessions". The row is a selector; the opener is "Resume conversation" in the detail panel, which on the phone is at y=791 in an 844px viewport, beneath the bottom tab bar.

findings.journey: Fork, edit and retry a turn — then find the branch again tomorrow
findings.what: Every branch is a top-level conversation, so one line of thought inflates the library
findings.evidence: After one base question, two retries and one edit the list header read "4 conversations" — rows "Base question · retry · retry · edit", "Base question · retry · retry", "Base question · retry", "Base question" — all created inside two minutes from a single prompt.

findings.journey: Cold start: orient and reach everything with Tab alone
findings.what: The composer — the app's primary control and the landing target of the skip link, every send, and every dialog Escape — has no perceivable focus indicator at either width.
findings.evidence: Computed on the focused textarea: `outline: "none 0px"`, `boxShadow: "none"`, `el.matches(':focus-visible') === true`. The only change is the `.composer` wrapper's 1px border going from `oklab(0.708221 0.0177785 0.0946424 / 0.45)` to `color(srgb 0.756863 0.603922 0.345098 / 0.45)`. Measured pixel diff blurred-vs-focused over the composer: desktop 1775/71820 px = 2.471%, max channel delta 39/255; phone 3705/145152 px = 2.552%, max channel delta 39/255. The app's own baseline captured the same way: rail 'Chat' 9.616% / max delta 203/255; phone 'More' tab max delta 208/255.

findings.journey: Cold start: orient and reach everything with Tab alone
findings.what: Escape from the command palette or Preferences does not restore focus to the opener; it drops to <body> and is then captured by the composer, 21 Shift+Tabs from where the user was.
findings.evidence: rAF focus trace after Escape: `t=0ms input:` → `t=9ms body:Skip to conversation Skip to compo` → `t=26ms textarea:Message Airship`. Opener was `"Open command palette"`. Measured return cost: `Shift+Tab presses to get back to "Open command palette": 21`. Cause is visible in the code: src/ui/platform-shell.tsx:145 captures `restore.current = document.activeElement` inside the post-commit effect (already <body> by then), whereas src/ui/mobile-navigation.tsx:96 hardcodes `const restoreTarget = moreButton.current ?? activeElement();` — and the phone's More sheet consequently restores correctly. The desktop's own comment at src/ui/platform-shell.tsx:785-787 names this exact bug ("dismissing the sheet dropped keyboard focus on `<body>`") for a third dialog while the palette and Preferences still have it.

findings.journey: Cold start: orient and reach everything with Tab alone
findings.what: There is no skip link to navigation, and on the phone navigation is the last thing in the document — so reaching Vault, Memory, Account or Proof from a cold phone load costs 25 Tab presses through the entire page.
findings.evidence: Only two skip targets exist: tab stop 1 'Skip to conversation', tab stop 2 'Skip to composer'. Phone chain measured: `mobile nav entered at tab stop 22: "Chat"`, `reached "More" at tab stop 25` of 25 total stops. The 11 destinations behind it (Editor, Terminal, Memory, Profiles, Skills, Capabilities, Vault, Connection, Account, Settings, Command Center) are all downstream of that 25th press.

findings.journey: Ask a question and listen for the answer
findings.what: The completion announcement is supposed to carry up to 200 characters of the reply and carries none of it on the default path every cold visitor takes.
findings.evidence: src/ui/chat/streaming-slot.tsx:66-79 arrivalAnnouncement() returns `Airship’s turn ended. ${prose}` and only falls back to the bare sentence `if (!prose)`. Observed value of that region, rAF-sampled: `t=1597ms [sr-only#1 atomic=true] "Airship’s turn ended."` — nothing else. The reply on screen at that instant: 'Airship is running this turn entirely on your device with the deterministic demo provider. Try /write notes/hello.md followed by content, /read notes/hello.md, or /ls.' Reproduced on the denial path too, where the announcement was again exactly 'Airship’s turn ended.' while the message read 'Permission denied for local /write-file. No tool effect ran, and nothing was sent to the model.'

findings.journey: Ask a question and listen for the answer
findings.what: Two polite live regions change in the same frame at turn end, so the kernel sentence and the completion sentence race — the precise failure the code was written to eliminate.
findings.evidence: rAF trace: `t=1597ms [sr-only#0] "Local kernel ready"` and `t=1597ms [sr-only#1 atomic=true] "Airship’s turn ended."` (phone: both at t=1566ms). The comment at src/ui/chat/streaming-slot.tsx:126-130 states the goal verbatim: "before this region existed, nothing announced that the answer had landed — the closest thing was the topbar runtime line saying 'Local kernel ready', a sentence about the kernel that carries none of the reply." That line still fires, simultaneously, from src/ui/app.tsx:8484.

findings.journey: Ask a question and listen for the answer
findings.what: The only in-flight utterance names a storage operation, not the model working, and is followed by 1.5 seconds of silence with no announced way to stop.
findings.evidence: The complete in-flight channel for a turn is one string: 'Persisting turn intent' at t=68ms, then nothing until t=1597ms. Nothing says Airship is answering, nothing reports progress, and no cancel/stop control ever appeared in the focus chain during the turn (focus sampled at 150/300/600/1200/2500/4000/6000ms was `textarea "Message Airship"` every time).

findings.journey: Run a command that fails, and find out that it failed
